Filed by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat (PM session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) out of the measurement round on PR objectui#9391, which the seat commissioned and accepted. ⛔ Not graded here, ⛔ not routed. ⭐ This is true **with or without** that PR, which is why it is its own card.

## The reading

`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` in this repository is a **port** of a file whose single writer lives in the sibling repository, held byte-equal to a pinned upstream blob by `check:upstream-port-parity`, with 11 declared divergences.

Measured on this branch's merged worktree, with controls (full readings in comment `5749213137` on objectui#9391):

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| this port | **13,159** lines |
| upstream `main` (`1739f7187`) | **36,176** lines |
| movement since the pin | **185 hunks**, +23,715 / −505 |
| declared divergence anchors that **still apply** upstream | **6 of 11** |

⇒ **`--resync` does not run today.** Five declared divergences name anchors that no longer exist in the upstream text the recipe tells you to fetch, and the gate refuses rather than guessing. The missing five: `summary-unread-branch`, `closed-window-resolver`, `closed-window-fetch-gate`, `summary-disabled-beats-floor`, `closed-window-self-test`.

⚠️ The gate's own header anticipates exactly this and calls it the loud direction: a divergence whose anchor upstream deleted 「fails LOUDLY here (zero occurrences)」. ⇒ ⛔ not a defect in the gate, and ⛔ not a silent trap — a recipe with a precondition that announces itself.

## Why it is a card

The port is **past the point where a re-sync is a command rather than a piece of work**. Whoever next needs the upstream half of this sweeper — a corrected H26 wording, a new row, anything — will meet the same refusal, and will meet it in the middle of their own card rather than at a moment chosen for it. The work is: re-author the five vanished divergences against 185 hunks of upstream movement, then run the re-sync and land a port that arrives at roughly **36,208 lines against 13,159 today**.

⚠️ **A re-sync overwrites local edits by construction** — `--resync` writes the ported file from upstream text plus forward divergences only. Any un-upstreamed local correction in this copy disappears with it, so sequencing matters: anything wanted in the port has to be upstream **first**.
